description: A portfolio manager must finalize the fund's tender-offer election for a portfolio holding and set the related recall, tax-reserve, and regulatory-filing actions, with input from compliance, tax, securities lending, and client coverage.

shared_context.S1: The fund owns 1,200,000 shares of Lydian Systems common stock.
shared_context.S2: Lydian Systems has offered $42 cash per share in a tender offer, and the board has recommended that shareholders participate.
shared_context.S3: The tender election must be submitted by May 20, 2026.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the final election for the fund. As part of the fund's normal corporate-action routine, Maya checks with compliance, tax, securities lending, and client coverage before submitting an election.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed this morning that the fund must attach a beneficial-owner certification to any Lydian tender election and file the related regulatory notice within 2 business days after submission; the rule was in a compliance memo not yet circulated to the portfolio team.

PF2.text: Elena confirmed in a tax memorandum received this morning that the cash consideration is subject to 5% withholding and that the fund must reserve exactly $1,512,000 for withholding on the approved 720,000-share election; the memorandum has not yet been added to the corporate-action file.

PF3.text: Ravi found while reviewing the lending ledger this week that 180,000 of the Lydian shares are currently on loan, and the prime broker confirmed that those shares can be returned before the election deadline only if a recall is submitted today.

PF4.text: Claire found the fund's client mandate side letter this week; it requires the fund to tender exactly 60% of its 1,200,000 Lydian shares, or exactly 720,000 shares, and the side letter has not yet been uploaded to the portfolio system.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 720,000 Lydian shares must be tendered.
A beneficial-owner certification must accompany the tender election.
The related regulatory notice must be filed within 2 business days after submission.
Exactly $1,512,000 must be reserved for withholding.
The 180,000 loaned shares must be recalled before the election is submitted.
The settlement must include commitments to submit the share recall and establish the withholding reserve.
The compliance rule requiring the certification and two-business-day notice must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the election would normally omit the beneficial-owner certification and regulatory notice deadline; PF1 changes those fields to certification required and notice filed within exactly 2 business days.
Without PF2, the settlement would not know the exact 5% withholding amount, which changes withholding_reserve_usd to exactly 1,512,000 and requires the withholding-reserve commitment.
Without PF3, the election could leave the 180,000 loaned shares unaddressed; PF3 changes the plan to require a same-day recall and the share-recall commitment.
Without PF4, the attractive offer could lead to a generic full or partial election, while PF4 changes tender_shares to exactly 720,000, representing 60% of the 1,200,000-share holding.
